newsitem.title: UK: European stocks eye records on dlr, Wall St.
newsitem.headline: European stocks eye records on dlr, Wall St.

text.p: European stock markets built on overnight Wall Street gains and the firm dollar on Wednesday, with new highs in London and Frankfurt encouraging investors on smaller bourses to ride the bandwagon.

In currencies, the dollar traded steady above 1.79 marks and 115 yen as the market awaited a German Cabinet statement reaffirming its desire for a strong deutschemark and euro single European currency.
Germany's DAX index showed no signs of giving up momentum as the blue-chip index set its sights on breaking 4,200 points by the end of the week.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, was up 30.06 points at 4,169.74 points, which was well above the closing level of the DAX at 4,121.13 points on Tuesday.
"The buy orders are coming into the market without end," said one Frankfurt dealer. "It's the same thing every day. There are no sell orders, only buyers from a broad spectrum."
Britain's leading share index, the FTSE 100, opened at a record high as investors continued to pour into banking and pharmaceutical shares in what traders see as a squeeze in the big-cap stocks.
At 0745 GMT, the FTSE 100 traded 22 points higher at 4,921.3 after opening at 4,909.6, boosted by follow-through buying from Tuesday when it set its second consecutive record closing high.
Technical analysts marked resistance at 4,930 as the index shoots for its sixth straight session of gains.
"We will be squeezed up further," one dealer said. "It's liquidity driven, whether it's mutual funds in the States, unit trust sales here, or pension fund contributions," the dealer said.
"Windfalls are being spent at stores like Dixons but a lot of it is also being channelled back into savings."
Bank stocks in London continued to show some of the strongest gains.
Wall Street stocks finished broadly higher on Tuesday, lifting the Dow industrials to an all-time high and propelling the Nasdaq composite index to its ninth consecutive record close.
The Dow climbed 53 points to close unofficially at 7976, the blue chip average's first new high in a week.

Technology stocks extended their dominance, with Hewlett-Packard Co ranking as the Dow's strongest component for a third straight day. High tech stocks in Europe were also seen gaining on strong second quarter results of U.S. computer chip maker Intel on Tuesday.
The Milan bourse's key indices, the all-share Mibtel and the blue chip Mib30, rose to new all-time highs in early trading.

Dutch shares were seen opening higher in nervous trade ahead of Friday's option expiry. Dealers said shares were a one-way bet after a higher close on Wall Street and the dollar steady at a high level.

The dollar was steady above 1.79 against the mark and 115 yen in early Europe after dipping overnight on German Finance Minister Theo Waigel's comments that the cabinet will make a statement on Wednesday calling for a strong mark and euro.
"Tomorrow we will say that we are for a strong euro and for a strong mark," Waigel told Reuters on the sidelines of a European prize-giving ceremony in the Bavarian town of Dillingen on Tuesday.

The British pound pushed higher against the mark on expectations of an interest rate rise, fanned by the published minutes of the June UK monetary policy committee meeting showing unanimity on interest rate policy.
Sterling traded at 3.0145 against 3.0178 late on Tuesday. CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar was at 115.80 yen and 1.7936 marks compared with 115.74 yen and 1.8013 marks in late trading on Tuesday. STOCK MARKETS AT 0900 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 40.3 points at 4,939.2.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 69.26 points at 4,190.39.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 32.75 points at 2,983.45.
PRECIOUS METAL
Gold was in London at $319.50, compared with a close of $320.05. Silver was at $4.32, against $4.33 London close.
